title: A sliced kit exports as a drum rack with one pad per slice, in order
description:
As a beatmaker, I want each slice of a sliced kit on its own pad, in order, so that the break plays back from the rack the way the score numbers it.

Runner and step vocabulary: `features/daw/kit-preset.feature`, `features/daw/STEPS.md`. Tests make tiny WAVs and manifests in a temp folder; no audio in git.

```gherkin
Feature: A sliced kit exported as a drum rack preset
  Background:
    Given a sample "brk.wav" of 2 bars in 4/4 at 120 BPM, analyzed
    And the score "flip.apr":
      """
      tempo 120
      key C
      clip brk = brk.wav
      kit b = slice brk by beats 1
      """

  Scenario: Each slice lands on its own pad, from C1 upward
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export succeeds and writes "b.adg"
    And the preset has 8 pads
    And pad 1 is on note C1 and plays "brk.wav" from 0.000 s to 0.500 s
    And pad 8 is on note G1 and plays "brk.wav" from 3.500 s to 4.000 s

  Scenario: Slicing by transients gives one pad per slice, in time order
    Given the sample "brk.wav" has transients at 0.0, 0.75 and 2.0 seconds
    And the score "flip.apr" says "kit h = slice brk by transients"
    When I export kit "h" from "flip.apr"
    Then the preset has 3 pads
    And pad 2 plays "brk.wav" from 0.750 s

  Scenario: The preset opens as a gzipped DAW document
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr"
    Then "b.adg" is gzip-compressed XML with a drum rack holding 8 samplers

  Scenario: The same score exports the same bytes
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" twice
    Then both files are identical

  Scenario: -o names the file
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "-o presets/flip.adg"
    Then the export writes "presets/flip.adg"
```
